questions.title: Have you identified and expressed any fears you have about dying?
questions.description: Understanding and expressing your fears about death helps reduce anxiety and allows loved ones to provide better emotional support during difficult times.
questions.help: Acknowledging fears is the first step to addressing them and finding peace.

questions.title: Have you considered writing a will, and if so, have you done it?
questions.description: A will ensures your assets are distributed according to your wishes and prevents family disputes. Without one, state laws determine how your property is divided.
questions.help: A will is one of the most important legal documents you can have.

questions.title: Have you appointed an executor for your will, and does this person know their role?
questions.description: An executor manages your estate after death, handling everything from paying debts to distributing assets. They need to understand their responsibilities beforehand.
questions.help: Choose someone trustworthy who lives nearby and is willing to take on this responsibility.

questions.title: Do you have a living will or advance healthcare directive in place?
questions.description: These documents specify your medical treatment preferences when you cannot communicate them yourself, ensuring your wishes are respected.
questions.help: Advance directives give you control over your medical care even when you can't speak for yourself.

questions.title: Have you discussed your end-of-life wishes with your loved ones and medical provider? What are those wishes?
questions.description: Open communication about your preferences prevents confusion and ensures everyone understands your values regarding medical care, comfort, and dignity.
questions.help: These conversations, though difficult, are gifts to your family and medical team.

questions.title: Have you considered what independence means to you, and how you can preserve it in your final years?
questions.description: Defining independence helps you make decisions about care, living arrangements, and medical treatments that align with your values and maintain your dignity.
questions.help: Understanding your definition of independence guides important future decisions.

questions.title: Do you have a plan in place for your pets or dependent loved ones for when you can no longer care for them?
questions.description: Ensuring continued care for those who depend on you provides peace of mind and prevents them from being abandoned or neglected.
questions.help: Pets and dependents need advocates to ensure their continued wellbeing.

questions.title: Have you discussed with your healthcare provider about the quality of life vs. length of life treatments?
questions.description: Understanding treatment options helps you make informed decisions about aggressive interventions versus comfort care based on your personal values.
questions.help: Quality of life means different things to different people - define what it means to you.

questions.title: Have you made clear what treatments or interventions you wish to avoid at the end of your life?
questions.description: Specifying unwanted treatments prevents unnecessary suffering and ensures medical care aligns with your values and comfort preferences.
questions.help: Being specific about what you don't want is as important as stating what you do want.

questions.title: Are there relationships in your life that need healing or closure?
questions.description: Addressing unresolved conflicts or expressing forgiveness can bring peace and prevent regrets, both for you and others involved.
questions.help: Healing relationships while you can is a gift to everyone involved.

questions.title: Are there any places you wish to visit or see one more time?
questions.description: Identifying meaningful places allows you to prioritize visits while you're able, creating lasting memories and achieving personal closure.
questions.help: Places hold memories and meaning - visiting them can provide comfort and completion.

questions.title: Are there any experiences you wish to have before your health deteriorates?
questions.description: Creating a
questions.help: Life experiences often matter more than material possessions in our final reflections.

questions.title: Have you expressed your gratitude to those who have been an integral part of your life?
questions.description: Expressing gratitude strengthens relationships, provides closure, and ensures important people know how much they've meant to you.
questions.help: Gratitude expressed is a precious gift that enriches both giver and receiver.

questions.title: Have you talked openly about your death with your children, or young people in your life, in a way they can understand?
questions.description: Age-appropriate conversations about death help children process grief, understand life's natural cycle, and feel included rather than confused or abandoned.
questions.help: Children benefit from honest, gentle conversations about death and dying.

questions.title: Have you considered leaving a written or recorded message for your loved ones after you're gone?
questions.description: Personal messages provide comfort, guidance, and connection after death, allowing your voice and wisdom to continue supporting those you love.
questions.help: Your words can provide comfort and guidance long after you're gone.

questions.title: Have you considered creating a video or photo album that captures memories and stories from your life?
questions.description: Visual and audio recordings preserve your personality, stories, and memories for future generations who may never have met you.
questions.help: Stories and images become treasured family heirlooms that connect generations.

questions.title: Are there any cultural, spiritual, or personal rituals you want to be observed towards the end of your life or after your death?
questions.description: Specifying meaningful rituals ensures your cultural, spiritual, or personal values are honored and provides comfort to both you and your loved ones.
questions.help: Rituals provide meaning, comfort, and connection to your beliefs and heritage.

questions.title: Are there any hobbies or activities that you have always wanted to try?
questions.description: Pursuing new interests while you're able can bring joy, accomplishment, and fulfillment to your remaining years.
questions.help: It's never too late to try something new and find joy in learning.

questions.title: Have you thought about ways to commemorate your life, such as a living funeral or life celebration?
questions.description: Planning your own celebration allows you to participate in honoring your life and ensures the event reflects your personality and values.
questions.help: Celebrating your life while you're present can be meaningful for everyone involved.

questions.title: Do you have a 'do not resuscitate' (DNR) order in place if you wish not to be revived in case of a medical emergency?
questions.description: A DNR order ensures medical teams respect your wishes about resuscitation, preventing unwanted aggressive interventions during medical emergencies.
questions.help: DNR orders must be properly documented and accessible to emergency responders.

questions.title: Have you discussed the option of hospice care with your loved ones and healthcare provider?
questions.description: Understanding hospice care options ensures you receive appropriate comfort-focused care when curative treatments are no longer beneficial.
questions.help: Hospice care focuses on comfort, dignity, and quality of life during end-stage illness.

questions.title: Have you thought about where you'd prefer to spend your last days (at home, at a hospice, at a hospital)?
questions.description: Specifying your preferred location for end-of-life care helps ensure you receive care in an environment that provides comfort and aligns with your values.
questions.help: Your environment during final days can significantly impact your comfort and peace.

questions.title: Have you planned your funeral or memorial service, and if so, have you communicated your plans to your loved ones?
questions.description: Pre-planning your service ensures it reflects your wishes, reduces stress on grieving family members, and can help control costs.
questions.help: Planning your own service ensures it truly reflects who you are and what you valued.

questions.title: Have you considered organ or body donation, and if so, have you registered and informed your family?
questions.description: Organ and body donation can save lives and advance medical knowledge. Clear documentation and family awareness ensure your wishes are honored.
questions.help: Donation decisions should be clearly documented and communicated to family.

questions.title: Have you decided who will take care of your digital legacy (online accounts, social media) after you're gone?
questions.description: Digital accounts need management after death. Designating someone to handle them prevents accounts from remaining active indefinitely and protects your digital privacy.
questions.help: Digital assets are increasingly important parts of our lives and legacies.

questions.title: Have you considered writing your obituary, or providing input for it?
questions.description: Writing your own obituary ensures your life story is told accurately and includes what you consider most important about your life and values.
questions.help: Your obituary is often the first thing people read about your life - make it meaningful.

questions.title: Have you thought about what you want people to remember about you?
questions.description: Reflecting on your desired legacy helps guide your remaining actions and provides clarity about the values and memories you want to leave behind.
questions.help: Your legacy is built through your actions, values, and the impact you have on others.

questions.title: Are there specific personal belongings that you want to gift to certain individuals?
questions.description: Designating meaningful items for specific people prevents family disputes and ensures sentimental objects go to those who will treasure them most.
questions.help: Personal belongings often hold more emotional value than monetary worth.

questions.title: Have you expressed your wishes for end-of-life care in the event of Alzheimer's or other forms of dementia?
questions.description: Dementia-specific directives are crucial because the disease affects decision-making capacity. Early planning ensures your values guide care decisions.
questions.help: Dementia care decisions are complex and benefit greatly from advance planning.

questions.title: Have you made arrangements to manage any business or financial obligations you have after you're gone?
questions.description: Ongoing financial obligations need management after death. Planning prevents missed payments, penalties, and financial hardship for your estate or family.
questions.help: Financial obligations don't end with death - they need proper management.

questions.title: Have you reflected on your life, your accomplishments, and what you've learned?
questions.description: Life reflection helps you find meaning, appreciate your journey, and identify wisdom worth sharing with others.
questions.help: Reflection on your life's journey can bring peace and perspective.

questions.title: Have you made peace with the fact of your mortality?
questions.description: Accepting mortality can reduce anxiety, increase appreciation for life, and help you focus on what truly matters in your remaining time.
questions.help: Making peace with mortality is often key to living fully in the present.

questions.title: Have you thought about the impact of your death on the world around you (e.g., community, environment)?
questions.description: Considering your broader impact helps you think about the legacy you leave beyond family and friends, including community contributions and environmental considerations.
questions.help: Your impact extends beyond personal relationships to your community and environment.

questions.title: What supplements or special dietary requirements do you have beyond those prescribed by a medical professional?
questions.description: Documenting your supplements, vitamins, and dietary needs helps ensure continuity of care and prevents harmful interactions with medications or treatments.
questions.help: Include over-the-counter supplements, vitamins, herbal remedies, and any special dietary restrictions or requirements.

questions.title: Have you found a way to discuss your death in a manner that feels comfortable for you?
questions.description: Finding comfortable ways to discuss death reduces anxiety and helps you have important conversations with loved ones about your wishes and feelings.
questions.help: Open, comfortable discussion about death benefits both you and your loved ones.
